{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**To:** Deal team (Customer)  
**From:** In-house counsel  
**Re:** Playbook review of Vendor's Master Services Agreement  
**Privileged & confidential — attorney work product**

---

## 1. Executive summary

We reviewed the MSA against the playbook and identified **19 findings: 8 deviations and 11 compliant positions**. The agreement is unusually polarised — several provisions sit at or above our preferred position (ownership of Deliverables and Customer Data, assignment and change of control, convenience termination, audit, governing law, renewal mechanics, insurance, and the absence of any MFN, no-hire or liquidated-damages exposure), while a discrete set of clauses fall into walk-away territory and cannot be accepted as drafted.

Three deviations are **critical or structural**: Section 20 contains a one-way, unlimited Customer indemnity with no Vendor indemnity at all; Section 21.1 caps liability at one month of Fees "without exception," which is below our walk-away floor and purports to override the Excluded Claims carve-outs that the parties otherwise agreed in 21.2–21.3; and Sections 2.1, 2.2 and 12.4 impose a USD 6M three-year take-or-pay, full-term exclusive dealing, and a 24-month worldwide non-compete on us.

A notable feature of the draft is **internal inconsistency**. Section 12.3 expressly records that we have given no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume or no-hire commitment, yet Sections 2.1, 2.2 and 12.4 impose exactly those obligations. Section 9.3 cross-refers to infringement remedies under a "Section 20.5" that does not exist. Section 11.1 mandates immediate permanent deletion of Customer Data while 11.2 and 11.3 provide for 30-day return and certified deletion. We have flagged these conflicts because they support our redlines as clean-up as much as negotiation.

---

## 2. Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | **Deviation** | § 20.1 | One-way, unlimited Customer indemnity; no Vendor indemnity of any kind. Section 9.3 cross-refers to a non-existent "Section 20.5." We added a Vendor IP / breach-of-law / data-breach / wilful-misconduct indemnity with standard procedure and narrowed ours to Customer-provided content and our breach of law. |
| 2 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | **Deviation** | § 21.1 (with 21.2–21.3) | Cap is mutual and the exclusions regime in 21.2–21.3 is our preferred position, but 21.1 sets the cap at one month of Fees actually paid and "without exception" overrides the Excluded Claims carve-outs. Redlined to the greater of 12 months' Fees or USD 1,000,000 and aligned with 21.3. |
| 3 | Critical | IP — Ownership of Deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | § 14.1 (with 13.2, 14.2–14.4) | We own Customer Data and independently developed IP; Deliverables assigned on creation; Vendor retains only pre-existing Vendor Technology, licensed perpetually; joint ownership barred. Preferred position met. |
| 4 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | **Deviation** | § 2.2 | Full-term exclusive dealing on us with no performance-based exit; conflicts with § 12.3. Deleted, with a 12-month / single-category fallback offered if Vendor needs protection. |
| 5 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | **Deviation** | § 13.1 | Subscription grant is revocable at Vendor's sole discretion and excludes Affiliates and contractors with no path to add them. 13.2 and 13.3 do not cure the Services licence. Extended to Affiliates and contractors, made transferable per § 24, and revocation tied to § 13.3. |
| 6 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | **Deviation** | § 12.4 | 24-month post-term, worldwide, undefined-scope non-compete on us; contradicts § 12.3. Deleted; a named-product, in-term restriction with internal-development and acquisition carve-outs is the most we could consider. |
| 7 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § 24.1 (with 24.4) | We may assign to Affiliates and successors without consent; Vendor needs our consent and may never assign to a competitor; § 24.4 bars Vendor termination, repricing or acceleration on our change of control. |
| 8 | High | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties on Customer | Compliant | § 9.4 (with 7.3, 27.3) | No liquidated damages, penalty or early-termination fee payable by us; convenience termination carries no charge; force-majeure termination is "without penalty"; § 7.3 bars interest on amounts ultimately not due. § 2.1 exposure addressed under MINCOMMIT. |
| 9 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant | § 9.4 | 30-day convenience right, pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees, no penalty, and no matching Vendor right during a committed term. § 2.1's take-or-pay language cuts against this and is addressed under MINCOMMIT. |
| 10 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | **Deviation** | § 2.1 | Three-year, USD 6M take-or-pay with no reduction or termination right; contradicts § 9.4 and § 12.3. Narrowed to the fallback: current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, true-up instead of penalty. |
| 11 | Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | **Deviation** | § 11.1 (with 11.2–11.3) | 11.2/11.3 give 30-day data return in machine-readable format and certified deletion, but 11.1 mandates immediate cessation of assistance and immediate permanent deletion with no export. Replaced 11.1 with up to six months of transition assistance at then-current rates, deletion only per 11.2/11.3. |
| 12 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | **Deviation** | § 19.2 | 19.1, 19.3 and the repair/replace/refund remedy in 19.4 are strong, but 19.2 caps the Deliverable warranty at 15 days and then strips any correction or refund obligation — below the 30/90-day fallback. Extended to 90 days with 19.4 remedies preserved. |
| 13 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 22.1 | Once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, business hours, off-site where practicable via an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, Vendor-borne cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%, no direct system access. |
| 14 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 28.1 (with 28.3) | New York law, exclusive jurisdiction in New York County state and federal courts, no arbitration; the executive-escalation step does not delay urgent relief. |
| 15 | Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations | Compliant | § 12.3 (with 7.1, 8.3) | No MFN or best-terms obligation anywhere; pricing provisions contain no matching or most-favoured-customer mechanic; § 12.3 expressly disclaims any such commitment. |
| 16 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation of employees | Compliant | § 12.3 | No non-solicitation or no-hire covenant binds us; § 12.3 preserves hiring freedom from general recruitment and disclaims any no-hire commitment. |
| 17 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Compliant | § 8.2 (with 8.3) | Twelve-month renewals, 30-day opt-out, 60-day Vendor reminder with the deadline extended if the reminder is missed, and uplift capped at the lesser of CPI and 3%. |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | § 18.1 (with 18.2) | Meets every preferred limit (CGL 1M/2M, E&O 2M, cyber 5M, workers' comp, employer's liability 1M) for the term plus one year; certificates on request and insurance does not limit Vendor's liability. |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

The following clauses, as drafted, are in walk-away territory under the playbook. We should not sign without movement on each:

1. **No Vendor indemnity, unlimited Customer indemnity (§ 20.1).** A one-way, unlimited indemnity from us with no reciprocal Vendor IP, breach-of-law, data-breach or wilful-misconduct cover. The broken cross-reference in § 9.3 to "Section 20.5" indicates the Vendor indemnity was excised from the draft.
2. **One-month liability cap, "without exception" (§ 21.1).** Below the six-month walk-away floor and below the 12-month fallback, and it purports to override the Excluded Claims carve-outs the parties agreed in § 21.3.
3. **Full-term exclusive dealing (§ 2.2).** Exclusivity for the whole term with no performance-based exit.
4. **Revocable-at-will licence excluding Affiliates and contractors (§ 13.1).** Revocable at Vendor's sole discretion with no path to add Affiliates or contractors; §§ 13.2–13.3 do not cure the Services grant.
5. **24-month worldwide non-compete (§ 12.4).** Post-term, worldwide, undefined scope.
6. **Three-year USD 6M take-or-pay with no reduction or termination right (§ 2.1).**
7. **Immediate cessation of assistance and immediate permanent deletion of Customer Data (§ 11.1).** No export or migration support, and inconsistent with §§ 11.2–11.3.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Issue the redline** covering the eight deviations, with the following proposals: add a Vendor IP/misconduct indemnity and narrow ours (§ 20); raise the cap to the greater of 12 months' Fees or USD 1,000,000 and align with the Excluded Claims in § 21.3; delete § 2.2; extend the § 13.1 licence to Affiliates and contractors, make it transferable per § 24 and tie revocation to § 13.3; delete § 12.4; limit the § 2.1 take-or-pay to the current 12-month term, reducible with true-up; replace § 11.1 with up to six months of transition assistance at then-current rates; and extend the § 19.2 Deliverable warranty to 90 days with the § 19.4 remedies preserved.
2. **Lead with the internal inconsistencies.** Section 12.3 already disclaims the exclusivity, non-compete and minimum-volume commitments imposed by §§ 2.1, 2.2 and 12.4; § 9.3 cross-refers to a non-existent § 20.5; and § 11.1 contradicts §§ 11.2–11.3. Framing these as conforming clean-up should reduce friction.
3. **Flag the four walk-away positions we will not trade:** the Vendor indemnity, the liability cap floor, deletion of the non-compete, and a workable licence scope. Where fallbacks exist, offer them now — a 12-month single-category exclusivity, and a 12-month reducible commitment with true-up.
4. **Confirm the commercial inputs** before the cap and commitment positions go out: expected annual spend against the USD 2M/year figure in § 2.1, the Affiliates and contractors that must be covered under § 13.1, and the transition window our operations team needs under § 11.1.
5. **Preserve the compliant terms.** Sections 8.2, 9.4, 14, 18, 22.1, 24 and 28.1 sit at our preferred position; we should resist reopening them in exchange for movement elsewhere.
6. **Reconfirm on the counter-draft** that no amendment to § 21.1 narrows the § 21.3 Excluded Claims, and that any Vendor edits to § 12.3 do not reintroduce exclusivity, MFN, minimum-volume or no-hire commitments.
"}
